newsitem.title: HUNGARY: ADtranz says full success not seen until 1998.
newsitem.headline: ADtranz says full success not seen until 1998.

text.p: ADtranz, a joint venture of Daimler-Benz AG and ABB Asea Brown Boveri Ltd, said on Wednesday the full success of the merger will not be felt until 1998.

ADtranz president Kaare Vagner said in a statement that, "the full scope of benefits targeted by merging the respective railway activities of ABB and Daimler-Benz into the ADtranz group will become apparent in 1998."

The company, which was officially founded on January 1, 1996, said that in its first year of business, operating profits after depreciation were 129 million European Currency Units (ECU) on sales of 3.196 billion ECUs.
ADtranz, the world's largest maker of railroad equipment, also said it expected the railway manufacturing industry to grow for some years to come.

"After two years of above-average order intake for the whole railway industry, the market stabilised on a reasonably high level, indicating continued growth for the years to come," the company said in a statement.
At the end of 1996, ADtranz said it had an order backlog of nine billion ECUs and that during the year it had received orders of 3.043 billion ECUs.
Although no comparison figures were available, in 1995 ABB's transportation unit, which was used to form ADtranz, made an operating profit after depreciation of 207 million dollars.
Daimler's rail business which was spun into ADtranz reportedly made a loss of over 400 million marks in the year.
